```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Quick Review: Making a Line Chart

Let's do a quick refresher on line charts using WMATA ridership data, since a line chart will be part of your homework. This is daily bus and rail data from January 2024 through February 2025 (you may recall it from the midterm). We'll aggregate it to weekly totals so the chart is easier to read, then make a line chart.

### Task 1: Load the tidyverse and the data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

wmata <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dwillis/jour405/refs/heads/main/data/wmata_daily.csv")

head(wmata)
```

### Task 2: Make weekly totals

Daily data is noisy — weekends and holidays create big dips that make trends hard to see. Let's aggregate to weekly totals using `floor_date()` to group days into weeks, then `summarize()` to add them up.

```{r}
weekly_wmata <- wmata |>
  mutate(week = floor_date(date, "week")) |>
  group_by(week) |>
  summarize(
    weekly_total = sum(total),
    days = n()
  ) |>
  filter(days == 7)  # Keep only complete weeks

head(weekly_wmata)
```

### Task 3: Make a line chart

Create a line chart of weekly ridership over time.

```{r}
weekly_wmata |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = weekly_total)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly WMATA Ridership (2024-2025)",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Total Riders"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Answer this question:** Describe the trend you see. Is ridership going up, down, or staying flat? What are the big dips, and what might explain them? What would you want to know before writing a story about Metro weekly ridership trends?

Ridership does not stay flat. There is a visible peak between 2025-01 and 2025-7 and sharp declines clustered around 2026-1 before it quickly rises up after the lowest point. Something that could explain the increase around 2026-1 is weather-- does colder weather affect people's motivation to ride the Metro because it could mean waiting for the train in the cold longer? If the dips happen over the weekend or around the holidays, could it be because less people traveling to work or school? And since the peak occurs after 2025-1, maybe the increase happened because more people are coming back to school and work. The quick increase after 2026-1 may be attributed to people coming back from the holidays, too. Since ridership does not present significant increases or decreases (compared to the ones previously mentioned), maybe this trend is because there are not major holidays that demand more time off. 

If I was writing a story about Metro weekly ridership, I would want to know what holidays or events that would require less traveling (e.g., if the trend occurs around winter break, students using the metro would not be commuting as much and workers would be at home if their job allows them time off on winter holidays). I would also want to know weather patterns during these tines. If cold weather has an affect on people's patience, maybe they don't want to wait too long under cold conditions.
